citation.title: Two Independent Spontaneous Mutations Related to Anthocyanin-less Flower Coloration in Matthiola incana Cultivars

original_retrieval.storage: outside_repository; not required by offline builder

rights.reason: The retrieved publisher page did not establish permission to redistribute the full article.

original_factual_summary: All six studied white stock cultivars shared a one-base deletion in ANS predicted to truncate the protein. Two of these white cultivars also carried a 481-base insertion in bHLH2.
The petal chemistry and qPCR experiments reported five biological replicates. White petals lacked detectable anthocyanin peaks while retaining flavonols.

These commercial cultivar comparisons provide sequence and expression associations. They do not establish six independent pigment-loss origins or an allele-specific rescue. The two double-mutant white cultivars are related, and the comparison with a bHLH2-only mutant concerns a yellow cultivar.
curation_scope_unchanged: Material-specific species annotation; not an allele assignment to FCP photographs or evidence of environmental adaptation.
